newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher as Maof breaks 300.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher as Maof breaks 300.

text.p: Israeli shares surged broadly on Sunday, carrying the Maof index above 300 points for the first time ever, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 2.51 percent, or 7.16 points, to 292.08 on very high all-share turnover of 265 million shekels against 196 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 2.63 percent higher at 300.08
"There's renewed interest in buying stocks. The whole atmosphere is bullish," said Jonathan Ross, vice president of Nesuah Securities. "The market is happy."

Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities, said the rise was in part due to news that Merrill Lynch had acquired 19 percent of drug maker Agis Industries Ltd for 200 million shekels for distribution to clients.
Agis, the second most active share, lost 0.25 percent to 3,900 agorot on volume of 16.9 million shekels.

In addition, Doron said, newspaper reports said Britain's Cable and Wireless had bought up 11 million shekels of Bezeq Israel Telecom shares in the market. C&W controls about 10 percent of state-owned Bezeq and has been seeking to reach an agreement with the Israeli government over its future role in the company.
Bezeq, the main gainer on the Maof, surged 6.5 percent to 1,006 agorot.
Amir Eayal of Epsilon Securities said prices were being lifted by a flow of new money into the market.

"The market simply looks good and investors are rushing in," he said. "The mutual funds are raising more money and investors are very enthusiastic. There is not enough free float so prices rise sharply."
Tsur noted that the mood was helped by the record high for the Dow Jones Industrial Index reached on Friday as well as news of the resumption of negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians.
But Ross said the market was inclined to shrug off political developments.
"I don't think the political situation should give people confidence," he said. "But it hasn't affected sentiment in the marketplace."

Eyal added that the recovery of the primary market was adding to the optimism. "Last week the we saw several successful offerings which were all oversubscribed. This is another indicator for the market's strength," he said.
Ross said the market was being moved mainly by improved corporate profits and low valuations. He noted that after adjusting for inflation, the Mishtanim index had not reached its 1994 peak.
Koor Industries gained 1.0 percent to 31,403 agorot. Ilanot Batucha Investment House said on Sunday that Koor was trading at an excessive 25 percent discount to its net asset value.

Agan Chemical Manufacturers rose 3.0 percent to 9,476 agorot. In a report released on Sunday Salomon Brothers lowered its 1997 earnings per share estimate for Agan to $1.94 from $1.96 after the company reported lower-than-expected earnings in the first quarter. Salomon maintained its estimate of $2.17 per share in 1998.
The most active share was Bank Leumi, which rose 1.25 percent to 546 agorot on volume of 17.3 million shekels. Israel Chemicals, the third most active share, gained 1.5 percent to 432 agorot.
($1 = 3.42 shekels)
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
